overview: Argosy Minerals is an ASX-listed lithium developer whose flagship asset is the Rincon Lithium Project, a brine-based lithium carbonate development in the Salar del Rincon, Salta Province, Argentina, held via a 77.5% (earning up to 90%) interest in joint-venture operating vehicle Puna Mining S.A. The company also holds a 100% interest in the early-stage Tonopah lithium brine exploration project in Nevada, USA. Argosy is effectively pre-revenue at the consolidated level: reported 'other income' is interest earned on cash holdings, not product sales, and Rincon output to date has been limited to small spot cargoes sold by the JV.

business_model.summary: Pre-production resource developer funding a lithium brine project through an equity-accounted joint venture. Argosy advances cash to Puna Mining S.A. (the Argentine operating entity) via loans/cash calls that convert to equity once a cumulative US$135m Phase 3 funding threshold is met, at which point Argosy's interest rises from 77.5% to 90%. There is no meaningful consolidated revenue; the company's P&L 'income' line is interest on cash reserves, and spot lithium carbonate sales (80 tonnes in 2025, plus a further ~16 tonnes and a 60-tonne contract referenced in subsequent announcements) occur at the JV level, not as consolidated Argosy sales. Value creation depends on completing a Definitive Feasibility Study (DFS), securing project financing/offtake, building a 12,000tpa (expandable to 24,000tpa) processing plant, and reaching sustained commercial production.

revenue_streams.name: JV spot lithium carbonate sales (not consolidated)

business_model.customer_type: Prospective B2B (battery/cathode manufacturers) once in commercial production; currently spot/trial cargo buyers
business_model.geographic_mix: Asset base: Argentina (Rincon, ~90% of value) and USA/Nevada (Tonopah, early-stage); corporate domicile Australia; company reports in AUD

main_competitors: Rio Tinto (Rincon Lithium Project, same Salar del Rincon basin, ~$825m acquisition)
Arcadium Lithium (Livent/Allkem merger, large Salta/Catamarca landholdings, now Rio Tinto-owned)
Allkem-era Olaroz/Sal de Vida legacy operations
competitive_position.market_position: Small-cap junior developer, pre-construction; one of many juniors competing for capital and offtake partners in Argentina's lithium triangle, dwarfed in scale and balance-sheet strength by major diversified miners (Rio Tinto) and larger pure-play lithium producers now operating in the same basin

moat_factors.description: 8,606ha of tenements in the Salar del Rincon with an updated Total Mineral Resource Estimate of ~731,801 tonnes Li2CO3; hydrogeological modelling supports up to 45 years of brine abstraction at 12,000tpa

US$5m strategic equity investment from Amperex Technology Limited (ATL, a leading lithium-ion battery producer) with an agreement to negotiate a lithium carbonate offtake, providing a credible downstream partner
Pilot plant testwork (2026) achieved 99% lithium chloride purity and 94.4% lithium recovery, de-risking the process design ahead of DFS completion

Already executed several small spot sales contracts (80t + 16.1t in 2025, additional contracts referenced in 2026) demonstrating the JV can produce and sell battery-quality product, albeit at pre-commercial scale

weaknesses: No consolidated revenue or operating cash flow; funds the business purely from cash reserves and periodic capital raisings
Minority/non-controlling economic exposure structured through a JV rather than full ownership, with governance shared 50/50 on the Puna board (joint control, not control)
Small market capitalisation (~A$70-75m) limits access to low-cost capital relative to major-miner competitors in the same basin
No offtake or project financing yet secured; DFS still in progress with a construction-ready decision pending

History of large, volatile impairments/reversals (up to ~A$69.4m impairment in H1 2024, ~A$10.8m net impairment at FY2024, partial ~A$10.1m reversal in FY2025) reflecting high valuation uncertainty for the underlying asset

growth_drivers: Completion of the Definitive Feasibility Study (crystallisation unit basic engineering package targeted October 2026) unlocking a construction-ready 12,000tpa project
40MW medium-voltage power infrastructure project progressing from design to construction, removing a key development bottleneck
Potential formal offtake agreement with Amperex Technology Limited (ATL) building on its US$5m strategic equity stake
Expansion pathway from 12,000tpa to 24,000tpa (up to 23 years brine life) if EIA approval for the larger operation is obtained
Growing track record of spot lithium carbonate sales demonstrating product quality and market access ahead of full commercial production

Recovering lithium carbonate price environment in 2026 (spot prices reported to have risen from roughly US$8/kg in mid-2025 to over US$25/kg by mid-2026) improving project economics and financing prospects
Optionality from the 100%-owned Tonopah project in Nevada, benefiting from US critical-minerals policy support (e.g., Critical Minerals Security Act, domestic-sourcing initiatives)

business.description: No consolidated operating revenue; project value depends entirely on successfully financing, constructing and commissioning the Rincon plant

Argosy shares joint control of Puna Mining S.A. with local partner Pablo Alurralde; strategic and operational decisions require alignment, and full 90% economic interest only vests after ~US$135m cumulative investment
Reliance on a small management/technical team and on JV partner Pablo Alurralde's process expertise

DFS, construction and ramp-up all remain ahead; company explicitly cautions there is no guarantee results from process modelling will be adopted or that a positive feasibility study will lead to successful commercial development

financial.description: Going-concern note discloses dependence on raising additional funding, divesting assets or curbing expenditure; cash fell from A$13.9m (Jan 2024) to A$5.96m (Dec 2024) to A$3.6m (Jun 2025) before a post-period A$2m placement; FY2025 net current assets were only A$4.1m against continued JV funding obligations

Company has repeatedly raised capital via placements (e.g., 80,000,000 shares at $0.025 in July 2025, US$5m ATL placement at $0.14631/share in 2024); ~1.46bn shares on issue with substantial further equity likely needed to fund the estimated remaining capital requirement toward the US$135m Phase 3 funding threshold

Reports in AUD but holds significant USD cash and incurs costs in USD and Argentine pesos; large translation swings have driven material non-cash P&L and OCI volatility (e.g., ~A$17m FX gain in OCI in H1 2024 reversed by A$2.2m loss in H1 2025)

Carrying value of the Rincon CGU (exploration assets, advances and JV investment) is highly sensitive to independent expert valuations; swung from a ~A$69.4m impairment (H1 2024) to a ~A$10.8m net impairment (FY2024) to a ~A$10.1m partial reversal (FY2025)

regulatory.description: Project depends on Salta provincial approvals (EIA approved for 10,000tpa; further EIA needed for 24,000tpa expansion), Argentine mining, water and environmental law, and macro policy stability under the current administration
Value of Tonopah tied to evolving US critical-minerals policy and permitting regimes

macro.risk: Hyperinflation and currency risk in Argentina
macro.description: Company explicitly flags hyper-inflation and political risk in Argentina, interest rate movements and logistics disruption as macro-economic risks with limited direct company control

Project economics and ability to raise capital are highly sensitive to lithium carbonate prices, which have been extremely volatile (a multi-year price collapse from 2023 into 2025 triggered Argosy's large impairments, followed by a sharp 2026 recovery)

Large new supply from brine, hard-rock and DLE projects across the lithium triangle (Rio Tinto, Arcadium, Ganfeng, POSCO and others) could cap price recovery even as near-term forecasts point to a modest 2026 deficit

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Lithium carbonate prices fell sharply from 2022-2023 highs through most of 2024-2025 (contributing to Argosy's large FY2024 impairments) but have recovered strongly into 2026 amid tightening supply-demand balances; industry forecasts cluster around US$15,000-18,000/t for 2026 with some analysts citing spot prices above US$25/kg (~US$25,000/t) by mid-2026, and Fastmarkets projecting the market shifting into a modest deficit by 2026 after a small 2025 surplus. EV and grid-storage battery demand remains the primary structural driver.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High - lithium is a highly cyclical commodity; Argosy as a pre-production developer amplifies this cyclicality through equity funding needs and asset carrying-value marks
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - as a cash-funded, pre-revenue developer with ongoing capital needs, higher global rates raise the cost/dilution of future capital raises and discount rates applied to project valuations
key_input_costs: Reagents/chemicals for lithium chloride crystallisation and carbonate conversion
Skilled labour and technical/engineering services in Argentina

recent_developments.event: Pilot plant test work delivered 99% lithium chloride purity and 94.4% maximum lithium recovery, materially advancing the DFS program
Reported execution of an additional 60-tonne lithium carbonate spot sales contract; trading halt requested ahead of an associated capital raising
Announced significant progress on the 40MW energy infrastructure (33kV transmission line and transformer station) to power the Rincon Lithium Project via EDESA
Non-executive director Peter De Leo resigned from the board

Group returned to net profit of A$4.0m (vs A$15.45m loss in 2024), driven by a ~A$10.07m partial reversal of the prior impairment on the Rincon CGU and the Group's share of Puna Mining S.A.'s profit (largely FX-driven, non-cash)
Completed a A$2.0m placement (80,000,000 shares at $0.025, with 1-for-2 free attaching listed options exercisable at $0.04) to shore up working capital

JV executed two separate spot sales contracts totalling 80 tonnes plus an additional 16.1-tonne contract of battery-quality (>99.5%) lithium carbonate; cash fell from A$5.96m to A$3.6m by mid-2025 before the July placement

US$5 million strategic equity investment completed by Amperex Technology Limited (ATL) at $0.14631/share (15% premium to 10-day VWAP), with an agreement to negotiate a potential lithium carbonate offtake
Recorded a ~A$69.35m impairment against exploration assets, JV advances and JV investment; independent expert revaluation as at 31 Dec 2024 reduced the cumulative impairment provision to ~A$10.78m

guidance.as_of: FY2025 Annual Report (year ended 31 December 2025, filed March 2026) and subsequent 2026 announcements

items.period: Not formally dated; subject to feasibility, finance and market conditions

guidance.management_commentary: Directors state Argosy remains confident of achieving key upcoming milestones and is committed to building a sustainable lithium production company highly leveraged to forecast growth in the lithium-ion battery sector. The FY2025 going-concern note states directors are confident the Group will receive sufficient additional funding as and when required, while flagging that the ability to pay debts as they fall due depends on raising additional funding, partial/full divestment of assets, or containing expenditure to available funding.

bull_case: Strategic equity backing and negotiating framework for an offtake agreement with Amperex Technology Limited (ATL), a leading global lithium-ion battery producer, provides a credible downstream partner and validation of product quality
Technical de-risking is advancing quickly: 2026 pilot plant results (99% purity, 94.4% recovery) and a nearly complete 40MW power solution move the project toward a construction-ready DFS

Sharp 2026 recovery in lithium carbonate prices (from depressed 2024-2025 levels toward US$15,000-25,000+/t) improves project economics, financing conditions and the case for a positive final investment decision

Large resource base (~731,801 tonnes Li2CO3 Total Mineral Resource Estimate) with modelled brine life of up to 45 years supports a long-duration production plan and multiple expansion phases (2,000tpa to 12,000tpa to 24,000tpa)

Demonstrated ability to already produce and sell small batches of battery-quality (>99.5%) lithium carbonate ahead of full commercial production is a tangible proof point relative to peers still in pure exploration
bear_case: Company remains pre-revenue with a going-concern qualification dependent on continued capital raises; cash reserves have declined steadily (from ~A$13.9m to ~A$3.6m through 2024-mid 2025) and further substantial funding (toward a cumulative US$135m JV commitment) will likely require material shareholder dilution

History of extreme, largely non-cash earnings volatility (a ~A$69.4m impairment in H1 2024 followed by partial reversals) makes reported profit/loss a poor guide to underlying value and signals high uncertainty in the JV asset's carrying value

Full commercial production is still not guaranteed: DFS, financing, offtake and construction are all still ahead of the company, in a high-risk jurisdiction (Argentina) exposed to hyperinflation, currency volatility and political/regulatory risk

Joint-control JV structure (77.5% interest, joint board control with local partner) limits Argosy's unilateral decision-making and dilutes economic exposure relative to a fully-owned project, while the step-up to 90% requires substantial further capital deployment

Small-cap, thinly-capitalised developer competing for capital, technical talent and offtake partners against far larger, better-funded players (Rio Tinto, Arcadium/Rio, Ganfeng, POSCO) operating in the same Salar del Rincon basin, and remains fully exposed to a highly cyclical and historically volatile lithium price
